S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.

subtypes.Derailment or Loose Associations: A speech pattern of switching rapidly from one topic to another with no logical connection between thoughts.
subtypes.Tangentiality: Speech that deviates entirely from the question and fails to answer directly.
subtypes.Incoherence or Word Salad: Severe fragmentation of speech and sentence structure, making it nearly impossible to understand.
subtypes.Neologisms: Using made-up words that have meaning only to the individual.
subtypes.Clang Associations: Speech governed by sounds, such as rhyming, rather than the meaning of words.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder characterized by delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking and behavior, and negative symptoms such as diminished emotional expression and social withdrawal, with at least six months of disturbance and one month of active-phase symptoms. It typically emerges in late adolescence or early adulthood, but late-onset cases can occur, particularly in women and under medical or psychosocial stress. The course is often relapsing and remitting with variable functional decline, and impairment in work, relationships, or self-care is required for diagnosis. It is distinguished from mood disorders with psychotic features by the persistence of psychotic symptoms outside mood episodes and from brief or schizophreniform psychoses by its longer duration and broader impact on functioning.

patient.stressor: About a year before presentation, Mark’s long-time regional manager retired and the chain rolled out a new inventory and scheduling system that shifted much of the forecasting responsibility onto store-level supervisors. The transition meant longer hours, tighter performance metrics, and pressure to manage abrupt schedule changes during a particularly demanding holiday season. Over the following months, his once-reliable ability to juggle complex staffing plans and inventory projections began to fall apart, leading to missed orders, chaotic shift coverage, and noticeable friction with both upper management and his associates. When his employer formally wrote him up after a series of disorganized staff meetings and customer complaints, his wife and adult son pushed for a psychiatric evaluation, recognizing that his decline in organization and judgment was far beyond normal job stress or aging.
patient.chief_complaint: “My wife says I’ve been acting all over the place at work and at home, like I can’t control what I’m doing or keep it appropriate to what’s going on.”

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.
S021.manifestation: When I try to explain a simple thing, like why the schedule got messed up, I’ll start talking about the new system and then suddenly I’m off on this whole track about barcodes turning into patterns and my mouth can’t seem to get back to the point, so people just stare at me like I’m speaking nonsense even though it all connects in my head at the time.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: Lately at the store and even at home I’ll catch myself pacing in tight circles, flapping my hands or freezing in weird positions in the middle of a conversation, and if someone asks me to stop or sit down I either don’t move at all or I’ll laugh and repeat the last thing they said under my breath over and over, like I’m not really in control of my body or how I’m acting in front of people.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Over this past year I’ve gone from running one of the steadier stores in the district to getting written up for chaotic shifts and missed orders, and at home my wife and son say they can’t rely on me for basic things like paying bills on time or following through on simple plans because I get too mixed up and odd in my behavior.
add_requirements.duration: Ever since the new inventory and scheduling system was rolled out about a year ago, I’ve felt myself gradually coming apart in how I think and handle things both at work and at home.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: For about the last six months, the way my thoughts and actions come out so jumbled and inappropriate has been clearly off the rails and not just normal work stress or getting older.
